main_text.l: Decimum nostrum Argumentum, ex parte Christi meritis, adversus Pontificiorum ultimum propugnaculum, seu potius latibulum defensionis suae: viz.
Quaestionis status de nostra virtute me-
accepta Deo reddi fideli-ter credunt, & palam constan-ter

profitentur: Pontificii vero, propriis Meritis Christi diffisi, (ut statim patebit) suam peculiarem merendi virtutem, tanquam ex ejus Meritis sibi indultam, commini-scuntur. Adversarios ipsos audiamus aequam est. {f} Stapletonus, Christus, inquit, nobis meruit virtutem merendi. A qua cantilena {t} Bellarmi-nus didicit illam suam, Merita nostra innituntur [?]

page.notes: The first part of the first line is set in a large woodcut initial P, joined to "Rotestantes" as "PRotestantes". The marginal notes are keyed to the text marks f and t. "innituntur" is the most doubtful reading; the line is heavily worn and the word may read differently. The text breaks off at the foot of the column and continues on the next page. Catchword "Meritis" is at lower right. The top right corner carries faint show-through, which was ignored. The left edge of the facing page was excluded.
